title: MCP for agent-to-agent comms may be the riskiest protocol you've never heard of
gist: Researcher Syed Anas Mohiuddin found 'protocol pivoting' vulnerabilities in MCP-based agent systems at Google, JP Morgan Chase, Rapid7 and others, where a prompt injection into one lightly guarded agent propagates to trusted downstream agents, often yielding SSRF; experts say agentic architectures have abandoned zero trust.

insights.claim: In the past five months, Google and four other unrelated organizations acknowledged vulnerabilities in which a compromised internal AI agent spreads harmful instructions to other trusting agents via MCP.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Agent-to-agent trust is a systemic, cross-industry attack surface, not a one-off bug.
insights.quote: Google and four other organizations—with little in common except for their use of AI agents—have acknowledged vulnerabilities

insights.claim: The attack targets a special-purpose agent (e.g., translation or data analysis) rather than the LLM; such agents often have lax guardrails and forward instructions down the chain to agents that explicitly trust them.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: LLM-level safety does not protect multi-agent systems; security must be enforced at each agent boundary.
insights.quote: The technique is a special form of prompt injection that targets not the LLM but a particular agent

insights.claim: Because MCP servers store credentials for each agent and agents trust all internal agents, exploits that the LLM would reject succeed, frequently resulting in server-side request forgery.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Credential concentration in MCP servers makes them high-value targets.
insights.quote: since MCP servers store credentials for each agent—and agents are built to trust every other internal agent—an exploit that would have been rejected by the LLM succeeds.

insights.claim: Syed defines 'protocol pivoting' as gaining access through one protocol, exploiting trust assumptions between protocols, and escalating to capabilities reachable only via another protocol such as Google's A2A or the Agent Network Protocol.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Multi-protocol agent stacks multiply trust boundaries where authorization gets lost.
insights.quote: a multi-step attack in which an adversary gains initial access through one protocol, exploits trust assumptions between protocols
insights.locator: Syed is calling the class of attack

insights.claim: X41 D-Sec's Markus Vervier argues 'protocol pivoting' is simply a subclass of indirect prompt injection, as cross-protocol delivery isn't strictly required, though he agrees it is hard to mitigate.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Whatever the label, the underlying problem is unsolved indirect prompt injection.
insights.quote: For me this is indirect prompt injection,
insights.locator: “For me this is indirect prompt injection

insights.claim: Google's MCP Toolbox for Databases vulnerability rated 8 in severity: its HTTP client lacked a CheckRedirect policy and didn't validate target IPs, letting a crafted path parameter redirect requests to internal endpoints.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Even Google's own MCP tooling shipped without basic SSRF guards.
insights.quote: A crafted path parameter could make the toolbox follow a redirect to an internal endpoint and send requests on the attacker’s behalf,

insights.claim: Syed says Google's fix—IP allow/block lists and rejecting unsafe base URLs at startup—is what a real SSRF guard looks like and more than most MCP servers have done.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Implies most MCP servers in the wild remain exposed to SSRF.
insights.quote: That is what a real SSRF guard looks like. It is also more work than most MCP servers have done.

insights.claim: The Rapid7 flaw (CVE-2026-97228) carried a severity rating of only 2.7 out of 10 and was fixed last month.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Severity varies widely by deployment; the class matters more than individual CVEs.
insights.quote: CVE-2026-97228, the vulnerability Syed found in Rapid7’s network, carried a severity rating of only 2.7 out of 10.

themes.theme: Zero trust abandoned in agentic rush

insights.claim: The article argues MCP became ubiquitous before being sufficiently tested and hardened, and that organizations rushing to build sprawling agentic architectures abandoned zero-trust principles.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Expect demand for agent security, authorization and zero-trust tooling as incidents accumulate.
insights.quote: MCP is new and is already everywhere before it has been sufficiently tested and hardened.
insights.locator: The fact that the pivoting technique worked

insights.claim: Rapid7's Douglas McKee says each protocol was built assuming it lived alone, so each checks its own front door while nobody watches the 'hallway' between agents, and every component behaves as designed—making detection hard.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Inter-agent traffic monitoring is an underserved security category.
insights.quote: Each protocol was built assuming it lived on its own, so each one checks its own front door while nobody watches the hallway in between.
insights.locator: “AI agents give attackers a fresh set

insights.claim: McKee advises treating anything passed from an LLM to a tool like input from an Internet stranger; the underlying bugs (injection, SSRF) and their fixes haven't changed in 20 years.
insights.speaker: Dan Goodin
insights.so_what: Classic appsec controls remain the main defense for agent stacks.
insights.quote: anything passed from an LLM to your tool should be treated like input from a stranger on the Internet
